subject: Advance Billing & Refund Scenarios for Atlas Health - Multi-year Prepay Options
messages:
From: Taylor Hughes <taylor.hughes@atlashealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Advance billing options for pilot -> enterprise rollup

Aisha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Atlas is excited about the latency/throughput profile you showed. Procurement has asked me to model a few advance-billing scenarios so finance can see the cash/GAAP implications. High-level ask: we expect a 3-year adoption plan that ramps usage (year1 ~40% of committed tokens, year2 ~70%, year3 ~100%). We want to understand:

- Term discounts you can offer for 1/2/3-year prepay buckets (annual vs multi-year upfront)
- How refunds would be handled if we reduce committed capacity or terminate early (pro-rata refund vs amortized credit)
- Any ramp schedule or true-up mechanics (quarterly true-up? crediting?)

Can you send the scenarios with a few concrete examples (numbers) and the contract clauses you expect for early termination/refund? Also, can these sync with our existing SaaS contract co-term on 12/31/2027?

—Taylor
Head of Platform Partnerships
Atlas Health

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Hughes <taylor.hughes@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Sasha Roman <sasha.roman@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Advance billing options for pilot -> enterprise rollup

Taylor —

Great to hear — attaching a spreadsheet with three illustrative packages and two alternative early-exit calculations. Summary below; spreadsheet has line-by-line math.

Option A (Annual prepay renewals, 12-mo invoice): 10% discount for annual prepay paid at start of year; quarterly true-up where we bill/credit usage above/below committed.

Option B (3-year upfront): 18% effective discount applied to total spend if fully prepaid at T0; automatic annual commit reconciliation with credits applied to following year.

Refund mechanics we modeled:
- Pro-rata refund: unearned portion of prepay returned less administrative termination fee (10% of remaining balance) — quicker cash repay, higher net refund to customer.
- Amortized credit: prepay amortized monthly over the contract term; early termination leaves any unamortized prepayment as a credit on final invoice (often yields no cash refund).

Quick example in sheet: $1.5M total for 3 years (3x $500k annual list before discount). If Atlas prepays $1.5M and terminates after 9 months, pro-rata refund = remaining 27 months of service value prorated less 10% fee (~$1.125M - fee). Amortized approach yields a smaller/no cash refund because most of the prepay has been recognized as balance.

You asked about co-terming — we can align billing to 12/31/2027 but that affects amortization and recognition; will include two co-terming approaches (rebate vs invoice offset).

Looping in Ben (legal) and Lauren (finance) to confirm acceptable clause language and any accounting concerns. If you prefer, we can propose two contract language options for early termination (cash refund vs credit-only) and you can pick.

I'll stand up a short redline call if legal wants to discuss specifics.

Thanks,
Aisha
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Taylor Hughes <taylor.hughes@atlashealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Roman <sasha.roman@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 12:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Advance billing options for pilot -> enterprise rollup

Aisha —

This is exactly what we needed, thanks. A few clarifying questions after a quick pass of the spreadsheet:

1) Under Option B (3-year upfront) the sheet shows an 18% discount. Is that contingent on a single upfront wire, or can we do a 2-pay schedule (60% up front, 40% at year2 start) and keep the discount?

2) For pro-rata refunds, can the termination fee be capped (e.g., max $100k)?

3) For co-terming: we prefer a true cash refund if we downsize; credits are messy for internal accounting. Would Redwood accept cash repay in principle if we agree to a 60% minimum usage threshold?

Happy to set a 30-minute call if that makes discussion easier.

Best,
Taylor
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Hughes <taylor.hughes@atlashealth.com>, Sasha Roman <sasha.roman@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 14:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Advance billing options for pilot -> enterprise rollup

Ben/Lauren —

Thread from Atlas (above). They asked about: 2-pay for multi-year discount, capping termination fee, and preference for cash refunds vs credits with a 60% usage floor. Can you please advise:

- Ben: are we comfortable with a capped termination fee (e.g., max $100k) in the 3-year upfront scenario? If so, what redline would we propose?
- Lauren: from an AR/revenue recognition perspective, would a capped cash refund break our revenue recognition assumptions (ASC 606) for prepayments? Also confirm whether a 2-pay schedule with preservation of the multi-year discount is okay.

I suggest two redline options in contract: (1) Pro-rata cash refund less min(10% of remaining, $100k) OR (2) Amortized prepayment with credit-only refund and termination fee waived. Please weigh in.

Thanks — Aisha
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Advance billing options for pilot -> enterprise rollup

Aisha —

High level: we can accept a capped termination fee. Draft language I would propose: "If Customer terminates the Agreement without cause, Redwood will refund the unearned portion of any prepayment within 45 days, subject to a termination fee equal to the lesser of 10% of the unearned prepayment or USD 100,000. Refunds will be paid in USD and will be net of any undisputed amounts owed by Customer."

Two-pay schedule: legally fine; commercial team should control discount triggers. Suggest we require at least 60% initial payment to qualify for the 3-year discount.

Lauren — any accounting red flags?

—Ben
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Hughes <taylor.hughes@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 16:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Advance billing options for pilot -> enterprise rollup

Aisha/Ben/Taylor —

Accounting note: a capped cash refund is workable but requires we recognize revenue in a way that preserves an appropriate liability for the refundable portion. For a 3-year upfront payment we would amortize revenue monthly, and maintain a contract liability for the unearned portion. If we accept the capped refund, we need a short memo documenting the refund cap and the assumptions for the liability release schedule for audit.

2-pay schedule: acceptable if a minimum 60% initial payment is received and the remaining 40% is due 12 months later with a default clause. We cannot apply the full 18% discount if payment terms are stretched beyond 12 months unless finance signs off on accelerated recognition.

I'll prepare a one-page accounting memo to attach to the contract package and can join a redline call.

—Lauren
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
